Definition: Mithredath, the name of two Persians
BiblicalUsage: Mithredath is the name of two Persians. The first was the treasurer who handed the temple vessels back to Sheshbazzar by the order of Cyrus, and the second wrote to Artaxerxes with the enemies of Judah to stop the building.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the two men show the two hands of empire: one hand returns what was stolen, and the other writes letters to stop the work, and God uses both.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile
